utterances.text: The then organisation of the military and political -- and military authorities did not make it incumbent on the military authorities to inform the civilian authorities about their own activities. The only thing that had to do with the life and safety of the citizens, I don't know whether they were regulated on the basis of a document of any kind, but anyway they were placed on our table to discuss and deal with. The civilian authorities and representatives of the military authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Isn't it true that, in fact, if such a threat was imminent that you should have taken the necessary measures to protect the population of Zepa. And when I talk about "you" I mean the civilian authorities as well as the military authorities.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what we could have done, we being the civilian authorities. In fact, we couldn't have done anything. That was the kind of situation it was, and the relationships that prevailed. Our place within a system. So that according to what I know, nothing more could be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Would it not have been normal to inform the civilian population not to gather, not to leave their homes? Would it not have been normal to let them know that there is a threat of an attack?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like this, you see: At that time at that place, even if you wanted to inform people you would have to go from house to house and inform everyone, tell them not to go out, to go outside. That would have been superfluous because the people had experienced war for already a year. The shelling in -- in 1992 and 1993, all that had gone before. And they're villages, after all. It's not an urban area where you have -- where life is organised in a different way. And you didn't have the firm distinction between the civilians and the army. The army members were incorporated into the other, because in 1995 everybody had some military activities, but they would leave from their own homes. There wouldn't be a barracks or anything like that. So it wasn't such a big distinction.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that the headquarters of the brigade were in the centre of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could just have a time-frame to orient the question, that's all, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about May and June of 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, according to my recollections, I think the answer would be yes for May. They were the offices of Colonel Palic and perhaps some others -- for some other activities. But it wasn't a building with all the amenities, logistics and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you ever ask Avdo Palic to move the headquarters of his brigade from the centre, so that the brigade is not situated in the centre of an inhabited area?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that we ever discussed the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that, in fact, you did not ask him to do so because Zepa was not shelled up until the month of July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like this: May 1993, until June 1995, there were hardly any military activities at all. And what you referred to as the brigade headquarters, that was just one or two small rooms in which -- or to which Colonel Palic happened to drop by. And the communications centre later on was in one of those rooms. And there was no need for any discussion of displacement or moving, as you call it, the brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit 5D249, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document of the Zepa Brigade dated the 4th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And according to this document the Chetniks, and I'm just quoting basically what we can read in this document, that the Chetniks did not have any activities in the last 24 hours, and that there had not been any shelling or any shooting in the area of responsibility of the brigade. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Such a calm situation [overlapping interpretation] respond to the situation as it was at the end of June to mid-July?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: End of July? This document is dated the 4th of July, 1995. So this was two days before the attack on Srebrenica. And this situation does correspond to the situation as I remember it. Because I can even remember an UNHCR convoy arriving in Zepa, possibly on this very day.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, just to confirm there must have been an error. I was talking about the beginning of July. So can you -- yes, can you confirm that such a calm situation existed in June and the beginning of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just remember the shelling of a village, I think it was Pripecak across the Drina, the Visegrad municipality and I think that this occurred maybe at the same time as the attack on Srebrenica. Now whether it was a bit before that. In any event it was before the beginning the "official" military attacks on Zepa. But in general terms, from May 1993 through 1994, and the first half of 1995, the situation was without -- I wouldn't say any activity, but any significant military activities on the part the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You mentioned a humanitarian aid convoy, and I wanted to ask you a few questions about that. During the hearing on the 29th of March, 2007, you said that in 1993 a consensus of the population was organised in order to have a distribution plan for humanitarian aid. Could you tell us whether this plan that you referred to was a written plan? Was it in writing?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember nor do I believe it was because we didn't really have any paper. We used what was left behind in the farming cooperative. We used the other side of the paper, there were a couple of typewriters. Whether, in the minutes of a meeting, this may have been recorded to have a census, I really don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you remember how humanitarian aid was distributed?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People would come to the centre of Zepa, and a team was working there. We organised things in the following manner: When a convoy arrived we see the quantities of goods that had arrived, and this would be put in warehouses, prepared in advance, and then we would meet and make a plan of distribution of aid arriving in that convoy. So if so much flour had arrived, and there were so many inhabitants, then we would know per capita or per family. If a family has five members, they would receive so much, depending on the amount available. General speaking we didn't make any reserves of food, et cetera, because it was best to distribute it to everyone, because we wouldn't know what to do with these goods if they were left in the warehouses of the Zepa authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that a part of the humanitarian aid was given to the army?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On our part, on our side, you mean, on the part of the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yes, sir. On your part, on the part of the civilian authorities, yes.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps these things started at the beginning of 1995 for a part to be set aside for the army. As far as I remember, earlier on there was no need for this because every civilian is also a "soldier" so that the distribution was done by families.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Why did the local government allow humanitarian aid to be allotted to the army?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, if there were such instances, and I assume there were, I'm trying to refresh my memory, these were small quantities. It may have been a request from the army for aid to be extended in certain activities. But this was something, as far as I remember, that occurred in 1995 and not before.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: A moment ago we were referring to helicopters bringing weapons to Zepa. Do you know why these helicopters were not used to bring food and clothing to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, a helicopter has a limited carrying capacity, and from the standpoint of food, to use those helicopters for these other purposes would mean negligible quantities. And these were risky flights. And I believe -- I of course didn't take part in decision-making about what and how would be transported, but the delivery of food in this manner and other kind of aid would not "pay off."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you know that the Zepa Brigade was regularly financed by the authorities in Sarajevo and even by certain humanitarian organisations?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that on a number of occasions some money was received, or rather the army received this money. As for the amounts, as I said on the first day of my testimony, I don't know. I don't remember. A couple of hundred thousand German marks were mentioned as a quantity. This was in the hands of the headquarters. What was purchased with those funds, I don't remember. I didn't take part in this, and what I do know is from hearsay.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we show the Witness document 5D213? Sorry, 216. Sir, this is a financial report regarding the means received and spent by the Zepa Brigade. And this report is dated the 27th of June, 1995, and covers a period from January 1994 until June 1995. Do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show the witness the bottom of the first page?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: At the very bottom you can see that the total is 818.800 German marks. Does this sum roughly correspond to the information that you had about the financial resources of the Zepa Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that this is a little more than I assumed. Of course I didn't see a concrete report, nor did I hear about it. But this total sum, to me, appears to be somewhat higher than I had assumed was the amount that was received for the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown the last page of this document, page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm interested in is the person whose name you see here. Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The "calculation compiled by"?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And this is someone who was working in the Zepa Brigade, wasn't he? He was mobilised to the Zepa Brigade, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by his rank, yes. But he's just the financial officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we go back to the first page, please? Could we see item 10, please? Looking at this point 10, regarding the sum received from a humanitarian organisation which is indicated as 30.000 German marks?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says, so it means that is true. Now, which is this humanitarian organisation? I really haven't heard of it. I don't know which organisation that is, Bridge on the Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Unfortunately I can't help you with that. Have you heard, particularly during 1995, that humanitarian aid was the object of some misuse? That there was some abuse of it?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean were humanitarian aid? I did not hear of any such thing. I think that generally speaking humanitarian aid in Zepa was distributed in a very fair and transparent manner. Whether anything was done that I was not aware of, it is possible. But this could be only minor occurrences. As for 1995, I don't know. But generally speaking, there was full control and we did everything for all the aid to reach the entire population. And we did ensure that virtually 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown Exhibit 5D264?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, could you look at top left corner. It is said the General Staff of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, it is dated the 24th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And this document is addressed to the civilian authorities of Srebrenica, Bratunac and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you remember whether you had occasion to see this document?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I see it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown page 2 of this document? And the last paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In the middle of this paragraph you find the following sentence: "It is particularly unfavourable that there is no order in the distribution of humanitarian aid. Various forms of crime and black-marketing have developed, among other things, because there is no organised influence of the competent bodies in preventing this."

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, regarding problems with respect to the distribution of humanitarian aid, if we can call them problems, in Srebrenica, I have heard about these things as an inhabitant of Zepa in those days. But I can say with full responsibility, because it was under my control, that distribution of humanitarian aid received from the UNHCR and perhaps Medecins sans Frontieres was done in an honest and transparent manner and whatever was intended for the population was received by the population. As this sentence refers to the territory of Srebrenica, I too heard about this. Nothing official from anyone, but what the stories were circulating at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you hear of situations when members of the army or the police mistreated drivers of the convoys or the people escorting the humanitarian aid convoys?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in the territory of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something I absolutely have no knowledge of, because in principle full control of the entry and exit in the Zepa enclave was conducted by UNPROFOR. And, as far as I know, our police did not have any check-points or places where they could check the convoys and the escorts of those convoys. Therefore, I don't know of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You have no knowledge of a check-point at the Brezova Ravan held by the Zepa police?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that such a check-point existed, but for a time only. I think it wasn't functioning from the spring of 1993 until 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that it was functioning in March 1995?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I don't remember. Possibly. It's more realistic that it was then than before. That it was functioning then than before that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And since we are now talking about this particular check-point, do you now remember that there were some problems that the convoys had with the Zepa police at this check-point?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I am not claiming anything that I didn't see myself, but if there was any mistreatment of anyone or if anyone was treated incorrectly, members of the humanitarian organisations, this would be counter-productive for the population of Zepa. So the general approach was that we have to be very careful and that no conflicts should be provoked. And if there were any such disturbances or mistreatment, I don't know about it or I don't recollect it, but our general approach was that that act in itself would be counter-productive for the inhabitants of Zepa in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you agree that throughout the war Zepa had water-supply?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Water, yes. Because in the centre of Zepa there is a large natural source and as far as I know the surrounding villages too, where the people of Zepa were housed, did have this water-supply ensured. So water was not a problem in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you know that UNPROFOR was selling fuel to the people of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wasn't this covered by Mr. Josse and the witness, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partly, yes. But I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you have new questions, different questions on the same issue, of course go ahead, I will not stop you, but if we can avoid repetition, otherwise feel free to go ahead as you wish. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may rephrase the question, that would perhaps be simplest.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know that the 29th [as interpreted] division that was based in Srebrenica was being provided with fuel from Zepa?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The 28th division, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- did receive fuel from Zepa. I may have heard of this but I really don't remember those things anymore. As for your first question, I did hear that this was done at certain UNPROFOR check-points where fuel was being sold, and the local people were purchasing it. I didn't see it, but that was the story being spread in Zepa throughout that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Are you aware that an UNPROFOR convoy arrived in Zepa in June 1995?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June 1995, UNPROFOR? No. The forces were already there. Maybe there was a change of shifts by the Ukrainians. Maybe the question should have been of the UNHCR and not UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: No, sir. I'm interested in an UNPROFOR convoy, and I wish to show you document P2497. Sir, this is a document of Republika Srpska army, and of course you cannot have had any knowledge of this document beforehand. Can you confirm that according to the first sentence of this document the movement of the UNPROFOR convoy was approved by the direction in Zagreb via Belgrade, and to the enclaves, and the first enclave is Zepa?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My understanding of this document is as follows: Each of the UNPROFOR units had to have logistic supplies. And if I am reading this correctly, one of those convoys carrying logistics is the subject of this document. Because as far as I can remember, every fortnight or so they had to receive fuel, food, et cetera, because this is a group of people whose lives had to be organised.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And according to what you can read in this document, this particular convoy was approved?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You see all these UNPROFOR convoys, as far as Zepa is concerned, they were never announced beforehand to anyone, no one had any right to stop them, and as far as I know, they entered their protected areas. You might see them passing but you don't know who is passing, where they're going, et cetera. We would just observe this as the regular supplies going to UNPROFOR headquarters, carrying food, fuel, water, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, would this be an appropriate time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Fauveau. Yes, we'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, on the 29th of March, page 675 -- page 75, we were talking about a census of the population that took place in the month of July of 1993, and you said that in 1993 there were 9.000 inhabitants but that later, only 7.000 inhabitants were left in Zepa. Is it right to say that between 1993 and 1995 a lot of people had left Zepa?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, well, I can confirm that there was this population migration, and most of the people went in the direction of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit 5D201, please. It's the witness statement, and this document should not be broadcasted.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, this is a statement that you gave to the Prosecutor on the 19th of January, 1998. I would like you to look at page 4, the penultimate paragraph in B/C/S, and it's on page 4, last paragraph in English, please. Take a look at it. Sir, when you made this statement in 1998, or at the beginning of that year, you said the following: "[In English] In 1993 we needed to have a kind of census in Zepa because of the distribution of the humanitarian aid. We established that there were 7.000 people in Zepa." [Interpretation] So what I would like you to tell us is if, in 1998, you stated that there were 7.000 people in Zepa in 1993, and during the hearing of the 29th of March of this year you stated that there were 9.000 people in Zepa. Is it possible that your memory was, in fact, better in the month of January of 1998 and that when you made the census of the population in 1993 there were 7.000 people in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my memory was certainly better in 1998 when I made the statement, and it's just based on my memory that I know that there was somewhat more than 7.000 people. Now, when I said up to 9.000, I think that was accepted as being a definite figure, that there were 9.000, and I know that the figure kept cropping up, this figure of 7.000, from mid-1993 right up until the fall of the protected Zepa zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: During the hearing of the 30th of March you talked about attempts of the population to leave Zepa, and in connection with this I would like you to be shown document 5D259. And before the document is put on screen, I would like you to know that this is a document stemming from the War Presidency of Zepa. Sir, so this is a document from the War Presidency of Zepa dated 5 May 1995, and it talks about a possibility of an evacuation of the population of Zepa for social reasons. I would like you to take your time and examine this document, and tell me what you think of this document.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like this: More or less everything that it says here is correct in this document to the best of my recollections. 65 per cent were refugees or displaced persons, so that might have been a more exact figure, those who weren't locals. So if you were a refugee, you were not in your own home, and you were living in a problematic area from -- in all respects, then it was a very valid human desire to leave that place and go somewhere where it was safer. Now, I remember the pressure exerted by certain people. Well, his son might live somewhere like Sarajevo, for instance, so regardless of the situation in Sarajevo this person or people wanted to get out and link up with their other family members who were living elsewhere and change their place of residence. Because that wasn't their original place of residence. And as to this last sentence, well, I don't have that information myself. That was written probably without my -- well, not in my presence anyway, so I don't know about this. I'm not aware of this fact. This offer for negotiations about the displacement of people and their moving out, those who wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown page 2 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: While we're on page 2 of this document, what you see, this is a request made by the War Presidency of Zepa to the government in which they would like to know if it is possible to negotiate at a local level with Serb officers on -- or officials on social -- on evacuation on a social -- on social grounds, and to see if such a thing would be justified by the Bosnia-Herzegovina political government. Now, you already told us that you have no memory of such an offer by Serb officials. Now if you see this additional information, could you tell us if this document refreshes your memory as to such an additional offer?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember, I'm looking at these dates here, but I don't remember any of this, and if what it says here is correct, and I'm not saying it isn't, then it must have ended up with Colonel Avdo Palic. Now, the questions posed by the War Presidency of Zepa under A and B, they're general questions. The rules of the game were such that there were no negotiations at local levels without previous acquiescence of the higher authorities, and this was a rule that held true in all parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina for all sides. So that this question, this second question under B, whether this evacuation from Zepa would be justified, is -- well, they wanted to see what this would look like from the positions of the top-most authorities. Whether, at that point in time, to use the term, it might be counter-productive. So let me repeat, I really don't remember any of these offers for negotiations set out along these lines, and I can't remember having taken part in the compiling and creation of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown once again page 1 of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, as you can see, this document stems from the War Presidency, but it was sent by the Zepa Brigade. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like this, you see: The only way of communicating with anybody was -- well, that includes the civilian authorities in Sarajevo, was via this means of communication, the Zepa Brigade, which meant that every document from mid-1994 onwards, which was sent to Sarajevo, was sent this way. There was no other route, no other way of doing it. And so I assume that the heading is always the same. It says, "The BH Army, the 285th Light Infantry Brigade, Zepa" as it says in the top left-hand corner. And then it states the organ compiling the document and who the document is being sent to. So we didn't have our own systems of communication, separate ones. We had to use the only communication system in existence and that was under the control of the BH Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: While we're still on the same topic, the departure of the population of Zepa, I would like you to look at the document D284 [as interpreted]. [In English] 5D284.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, the document doesn't appear in the system.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to save time, could we maybe ask Mrs. Usher to place the document on the ELMO? I'm terribly sorry, the document has a different number. It's 224. Let's try not to lose any time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document stemming from the Zepa Brigade, and I would like you to tell us if you know the name of the person at the bottom of this page. Do you know whose signature that is, whose name that is at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know this person. And he was involved in the BH Army, engaged in the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: He was an officer charged of the security of the Zepa Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And according to this document dated 25 May 1995, a certain number of people, including civilians, women and children, left towards a free territory farther than Srebrenica, that is Kladanj and Olovo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the document itself it says -- well, the -- it is in the conditional, that's the tense used in the document. That it could, and then it says what should be done. Now, I don't know that in 1995 there were any -- there was any large-scale departure from Zepa towards Kladanj and Olovo. Whether people wanted to, quite obviously they did. That was the wish. And this document seems to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What I would like to know, what I'm interested in, is paragraph 2. According to this paragraph, the necessary measures or the measures that should be taken in order not to allow this departure are enumerated. I would like to know why is it that the Zepa Brigade wanted to stop women and children to leave Zepa --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: From leaving Zepa, correction.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like this: The departure of civilians with women and children leaving across the forest, that would be impossible. Perhaps we're thinking along the same lines. But in this way it was only the fittest men with arms that could leave the region who knew the terrain well. And I think that there is a slight contradiction here in the document itself. Because women, children and civilians are mentioned at the top of the document, and then this exit which would mean going on foot for 40 kilometres, passing through two military lines in the process. So the document itself, well I don't know whether it was shown in a previous testimony, but it doesn't represent anything special or separate and I don't think it reflects the actual situation because how could all these people move out? Civilians, women, children, that would have been impossible. It would have been mission impossible to traverse this terrain in that way. Now, why the 285th Eastern Bosnian Light Infantry Brigade didn't want this to take place, I think that refers to members of the BH Army, only them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Were you aware that members of the BiH army had fled to Serbia before the fall of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have that information, although of course in principle that that had happened, I would have had to know about it but I really didn't know about it and I didn't receive information of that kind, even later on. I never heard this confirmed by anyone, that is to say that before Zepa fell that somebody crossed over to the territory of Serbia, which was actually Yugoslavia at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit 6D74, please -- 64, please. [In English] 64.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is a document stemming from the 8th Operational Group of Srebrenica dated 25 February 1995, and this document talks about weapons. It's not the topic of my cross-examination at this point, but I would like you to look at the last page of this document, please. Can you see, and I will quote what I read in this document, "[In English] The enemy Chetniks found out about all the helicopter flights and MDS transport from Zepa to Srebrenica, from the deserters who deserted to the Republic of Serbia by telling the enemy everything about all activities." [Interpretation] Do you have any reason to doubt the truthfulness of this document that would have been written by Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like this: Everything I say is speculation, because I really don't have any information about this, of the nature contained in -- on page 2 underneath all the specifications for the weapons, what -- the materiel that probably arrived. So this is the first time that I hear of this. And it's something new for me too. Now, whether, with this sentence or these couple of sentences, at that time they wanted to express something else, to say something else, I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: During your testimony of the 30th of March, 1995 [sic] you talked about negotiations that you had with Serb officials after the fall of Srebrenica. Is it right that after the first negotiations that took place on the 13th of July, that Serbs offered you to evacuate all of the population?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have been testifying about that. It was a meeting with General Tolimir. I think I explained that. Do you want me to go back to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a few very specific questions. I would like to perhaps correct something that's written on page [as interpreted] 23, I wanted to mention the 30th of March 2007 and not the 30th of March 1995. I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that, but I knew what you meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: That Serb offer during this first round of negotiations also included the evacuation of men who were able-bodied, so able-bodied men. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I emphasise that. The offer on paper put down on paper, and also expressed orally, was to that effect. They said that everybody could leave the territory of Zepa safely.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: However, is it right that at the time you did not have the authorisation to negotiate or to sign any agreement?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before my departure to attend those negotiations we received permission to go to the negotiations without permission to sign anything, but to attend the talks and to see what it was all about. Because we didn't know what specific demands were being made by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Were you aware that the military authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and namely General Hadzihasanovic, was against the fact that you go and participate to these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, on that day, the 13th of July, in the morning, and let me repeat, all communication went via the communications centre held by the army. So most of those things we received orally, without any documents. As far as I remember, it was from two different places at our request that two opposing answers arrive. One in favour of us going, and the other, I don't know whether that was the military one, that was against, or whether it was the other way around. Which side was against and which side was in favour, but we decided to go and attend those talks anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit 5D275, please. Could you please scroll down? I'm interested in the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document as being one of the documents that you mentioned long ago -- [overlapping interpretation] we were speaking about just now?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this document for the first time. Could you please roll it down so that I can see the top of the page? But what I have said stands, there was a lot of confusion. Someone said we could go, someone else that we couldn't. I see this is the 13th of July at 10.50. I think that by then we had already left for the -- to attend the negotiations. If the time indicated is correct, as far as I can remember, by then we were already at the negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you agree that in this document, which was sent by General Hadzihasanovic, according to paragraph 2, the president of the War Presidency of Zepa should be informed that he should not go to negotiate with the aggressor?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is stated very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you know that when you had the second negotiations the Zepa Brigade was receiving orders from the headquarters of the BH Army to continue to fight?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the negotiations on the 19th of July?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the overall situation at the time, this is something I am not aware of because everything was chaotic, things were not centralised in one place where you could receive all the information. So that it is something I don't know, that there were any specific orders to continue the struggle. Because by then the situation was such that it required for us locally to deal with the issue. Each of those orders needs to be compared with the situation you found yourself in, and you had to make a decision on that basis, because, after all, the lives of the people in Zepa were in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown 5D270.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, this is an order, and we'll come back to the word "order." Anyway, it's a document dated the 19th of July, 1995 addressed by the General Staff of the BH Army to the command of the 2nd Corps, and to the Zepa Brigade.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no comment to make. This is information of the General Staff passed on to the command of the 2nd Corps, or rather the 285th East Bosnian Light Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown the very bottom of this first page?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that the last word on this page is the word "I order"?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we now go on to page 2 of this document, please? Sir, don't we see at the bottom of the page of this document the name of Rasim Delic, the commander of the BH Army at the time?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in paragraph 1 of this order is it stated that the defence should be organised and activities continued?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And when you were at the negotiations on the 19th of July, you didn't know that such an order had reached Zepa?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And did you know that after you signed the agreement with the Serbs the Zepa Brigade sent to President Izetbegovic a letter informing him that it was out of the question that the brigade members, that the soldiers of the brigade would surrender?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat for the third time, the general position or feeling was that members of the unit may not and will not surrender. I'm saying this perhaps for the fourth time. In principle I was aware of this position, because people feared for their lives.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said during the hearing of the 30th of March, pages 31 and 32 of the transcript, that when you saw General Mladic on the 28th of July, that on that day General Mladic did not greet you, and you interpreted this as being due to the fact that you were a prisoner. Is that what you told us?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less that is right. On the 27th we were sitting normally, and in the evening of the 27th, when I was informed that my status was that of a prisoner of war, and I went to Borak and was brought back, I was sitting with Amir Imamovic at Boksanica or near there, General Mladic passed by without any greetings. That is what I said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Would you agree that on the 28th of July, 1995, it was quite clear that the agreement that you had signed would not be respected by the Bosniak side?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think this has been asked several times in different shapes and manners. Let's go to the next question. Incidentally, since this is obvious that we will not be finishing with the testimony of this witness today, the other Defence teams, Popovic Defence team, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: We will have no questions for this witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Nor do we.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Only a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But it's obvious that we won't finish today. And will you have a re-examination as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. And I will engage in some discussions with my friends to see whether I can minimise that with the schedule, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So if could I kindly ask you to wind it up for today, and you will continue tomorrow, Madam Fauveau, because we'll need a few minutes to hand down an order relating to the intercepts that you have all been waiting for. Whenever it's convenient for you. I need about three, four minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we can stop now. And tomorrow I will need between 5 and 10 minutes, certainly not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. One thing is I hope that, after this witness, you've only got one, and that's 135? Because I wouldn't like the subsequent witness to start and then go home for the Easter period and then come back. I wouldn't like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's a bit late, the witness unfortunately, we had to make a call sometime last week to bring the following witness after the next witness in. I think Mr. President, you're correct, I don't think we are going to reach him, so unfortunately, we'll just have to send him back, but that's the reality we live with with our schedule, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. On the issue of the intercepts, and -- yeah, the witness can be escorted out. Witness, we will meet you again tomorrow. And hopefully we will be able to finish with your testimony in about 30 minutes, and then you are free to go home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So on the issue of the intercepts and following the debate that took place a few days ago, we have decided to proceed as follows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First, the Defence have proposed to put forward an expert witness at this time, in other words, in the course of the case for the Prosecution in order that the evidence can be considered by the Trial Chamber in reaching its decision on whether the intercepts will be admitted or not. The Prosecution has not agreed to this, however we are of the opinion that in the interest of justice the Trial Chamber should have the evidence before it prior to any decision on admissibility. Therefore, pursuant to Rule 85(A) and in accordance with the request of the Defence, the expert report should be disclosed under Rule 94 bis by the 23rd of April. The Prosecution then will have the 30-day period to respond in accordance with the rule, and following that time period, if necessary, arrangements should be made for the recalling of the witness as soon -- for the calling, not recalling, for the calling of the witness, as soon as feasible in terms of the court schedule. Roughly we have in mind on or around May 23rd, as you had suggested, Mr. Bourgon. We do not propose at this time to speculate on any possible applications that the Prosecution might wish to make or may make in response to such evidence. We will address any such issues if and when they are raised. Now, in regard, or in terms of the filing of submissions, we believe that it is not necessary to alter the schedule of submissions significantly. Therefore, the Prosecution will proceed with its submissions as set out in the original order of 7th March, which the four-week extension that was requested by the Prosecution on the 22nd of March. As you will recall, an extension was granted orally on the 27th of March, until the 29th of April. The Prosecution submission at this stage obviously would not address the proposed evidence of the expert witness, who would not have testified by then. The Defence will then have 14 days from the conclusion of the testimony of the Defence expert to file their full submission, including any related to the expert evidence. And finally, the Prosecution will then have 21 days to file a reply, including any submissions it wishes to make regarding the expert evidence. I hope this is clear and that it accommodates your respective requirements. We stand adjourn -- yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just if we could get an estimate from the Defence how long they think this expert will be testifying, because we have people coming in from gaols around the world that month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Mr. Bourgon, I trust you will communicate with Mr. McCloskey on this, you don't need to make a pronouncement in Chambers. Okay. Thank you. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
